items.title: Spain's Sánchez and rivals make final appeals before election
items.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his rivals held rallies in the final days of Spain's election campaign. Opponents accused Sánchez of dishonesty and betrayal while he seeks to defy unfavourable polls.

items.title: King tides flood Bay Area shorelines and break off part of Pacifica pier
items.summary: King tides and strong waves caused flooding along Bay Area shorelines, including San Francisco's waterfront and North Bay roadways. Part of the Pacifica pier collapsed.

items.title: Man arrested after $10,000 bracelet snatched from pensioner in San Fernando
items.summary: A 25-year-old Laventille man was arrested Thursday after allegedly snatching a $10,000 gold bracelet from a 68-year-old pensioner in San Fernando on November 26, police said.

items.title: US forces disable commercial ship accused of trying to breach Iran blockade
items.summary: A US military aircraft struck a Palau-flagged commercial ship with precision munitions after multiple warnings, US Central Command said. The ship allegedly tried to breach the US blockade of Iran.

items.title: Los Angeles schools block Google AI features
items.summary: The Los Angeles Unified School District blocked Google's AI features and is considering dropping the company's products. Google has threatened to cut schools' search access.

items.title: Hackers breach US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform
items.summary: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, Reuters reported exclusively. The breach follows reported attacks on the Treasury Department and the CIA.

items.title: Prosecutors seek 25-year sentence for Canadian man who aided 14 suicides
items.summary: Prosecutors are seeking a 25-year sentence for Kenneth Law, a former chef who pleaded guilty to aiding 14 suicides in Canada. He has admitted selling so-called suicide kits worldwide.

items.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed from Ibiza
items.summary: A capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel will be towed away from Ibiza. Its fuel tanks have so far remained intact amid fears of a major spill.

items.title: San Francisco police vehicle crashes into Mission District restaurant
items.summary: A San Francisco police vehicle crashed into a restaurant in the Mission District.

items.title: Sarah Wynn-Williams speaks about living under a gag order
items.summary: Sarah Wynn-Williams, author of 'Careless People' about her time at Facebook, described living under a gag order.

items.title: Thailand seeks source of river pollution from Myanmar mines
items.summary: Thailand is moving to identify the source of river pollution linked to mining in neighbouring Myanmar.

items.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok generating child sexual images and revenge porn
items.summary: A group of US states sued SpaceX to stop its Grok AI from generating child sexual abuse images and non-consensual intimate imagery.

items.title: Russian military flotilla bound for Libya turns back after warship sunk
items.summary: A Russian military flotilla headed to Libya has turned around after a warship was sunk on November 22, according to sources cited by Reuters. Ukrainian media attribute the sinking to a Ukrainian attack on the ships.

items.title: US opens cartel tip hotline in Mexico, drawing Sheinbaum's criticism
items.summary: The DEA set up anonymous tip lines in Mexico about cartels. President Claudia Sheinbaum criticised the move as interference by US officials.

items.title: Calls grow for AI guardrails as US retailers expand use
items.summary: Rising use of AI at US retailers has prompted calls for guardrails and regulation.

items.title: Reggae Girlz coach Busby denied US entry before World Cup qualifier
items.summary: Jamaica women's coach Hubert Busby Jr was denied entry to the US and will miss Friday's World Cup qualifier against Costa Rica in Texas. The denial was linked to his pending green card application.

items.title: Convex skills send users' app ideas to a remote server without disclosure
items.summary: A report says Convex's AI agent skills send users' app ideas to a remote server without informing them.

items.title: Zelenskyy calls Trump's friendship with Putin 'strange', urges more US pressure
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said President Trump calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" was strange because Putin is an aggressor. He said the US is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks.

items.title: Berkeley reparations coalition targets 2028 ballot
items.summary: A Berkeley coalition aims to put cash school reparations for descendants of enslaved people to a public vote in 2028, which would be a first for a California district.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader convicted over 123 more deaths
items.summary: Paul Mackenzie, leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, was found guilty of killing 123 more followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

items.title: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec religious symbols ban
items.summary: Canada's top court largely upheld Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public servants. Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers were among those who challenged the law as a violation of fundamental rights.

items.title: UN peacekeepers prepare to leave southern Lebanon after 50 years
items.summary: The UN peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon is preparing to end its 50-year mission, with no plan in place for what follows. Tensions between Israel and Hezbollah remain high.

items.title: EU leaders fail to agree budget, leaving Ukraine loan in limbo
items.summary: European Union leaders failed to agree on the 2028-2034 budget, European Council President António Costa said, leaving a planned loan to Ukraine unresolved. Leaders will try again in three weeks.

items.title: Brazil rejects Macron's description of its meat as 'doped'
items.summary: Brazil pushed back after French President Emmanuel Macron called its meat "doped" while addressing French farm representatives. The EU banned Brazilian beef and poultry products months ago.

items.title: Card-skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
items.summary: Researchers found credit card skimming scripts that use WebRTC to exfiltrate data on popular shopping websites.

items.title: Man found guilty of attempted murder of 14, including 10 on UK train
items.summary: A man with schizophrenia was found guilty of attempting to murder 14 people in three incidents over 24 hours, ending with the stabbing of 10 people on a high-speed London-bound train.

items.title: San Francisco fire displaces six people
items.summary: A fire in San Francisco displaced six people from their homes.

items.title: Four left homeless after Charlotteville house fire
items.summary: Four people lost their home after a fire gutted a split-level house on Old Scheme Street in Charlotteville, Tobago.

items.title: AI usage surges while spending stalls
items.summary: MarketWatch reports that AI usage is growing rapidly while spending on it is stalling.

items.title: Consumer groups warn against some learning toys for young children
items.summary: Consumer safety groups and early childhood experts are urging parents not to give certain learning toys to the youngest children.

items.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI restructuring
items.summary: Software company SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 positions as AI transforms the sector, according to sources.

items.title: Investigator says Russia is indoctrinating Ukrainian children at camps
items.summary: An investigator says many Ukrainian children taken to Russian camps since the invasion are barred from speaking Ukrainian and made to hear the Russian anthem daily.

items.title: Trump attacks opponents and threatens vetoes in Thanksgiving posts
items.summary: President Trump criticised opponents and threatened future vetoes in Thanksgiving social media posts. He also spoke to reporters about Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia and his recent meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.

items.title: NASA's NG-25 resupply mission to carry space crop production system
items.summary: Northrop Grumman's 25th resupply mission to the ISS will carry NASA experiments including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system. NASA is studying crops that could feed astronauts on Moon and Mars missions.

items.title: Iranian women face lashings and 'honor killings'
items.summary: Singer Parastoo Ahmadi received 74 lashes for singing without a head covering in Iran. Other women have been killed, some by their own families.

items.title: T&T refuses to back COP31 deal without stronger commitments
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago said it will not support the COP31 climate agreement without stronger commitments.

items.title: Endangered turtles found taped up in baggage at Amsterdam airport
items.summary: Officials found endangered turtles bound with duct tape inside baggage at Amsterdam's airport.

items.title: UN warns hunger will worsen in 16 countries
items.summary: The United Nations warns hunger will deepen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan and Yemen at greatest risk.

items.title: BAE Systems says European combat vehicle order totals $6 billion
items.summary: BAE Systems said a European order for combat vehicles is worth a total of $6 billion.

items.title: Intel pressed to give Trump administration 10% stake to unlock grants
items.summary: Intel faced pressure to surrender a 10% stake to the government in order to receive billions of dollars in promised grants.

items.title: California still lacks count of missing and murdered Native people
items.summary: California has no statewide count of missing or murdered Native people after Gov. Newsom vetoed a program as duplicative. Families rely on social media and grassroots groups.

items.title: Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape
items.summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on charges of rape and sexual assault, including the alleged rape of a young actress at his Paris home in 2018.

items.title: Volkswagen draws Mercedes and BMW into $1.2 billion India tax dispute
items.summary: Volkswagen has brought rivals Mercedes-Benz and BMW into its $1.2 billion tax dispute in India, Reuters reported exclusively.

items.title: Former media executive admits remark about abuse survivor Grace Tame
items.summary: A former Murdoch media executive admitted saying Australian child sex abuse survivor Grace Tame was "looking to be raped again," a comment overheard at an event about how she was dressed.

items.title: Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC, Reuters reports
items.summary: The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC, according to a Reuters report.

items.title: Former Kenyan governor jailed 25 years for murder of pregnant girlfriend
items.summary: A former Kenyan governor was sentenced to 25 years for the murder of his pregnant girlfriend, a student killed after meeting a journalist to discuss their affair.

items.title: Suspect arrested in fatal Tenderloin shooting
items.summary: Police arrested a suspect in a fatal shooting in San Francisco's Tenderloin.

items.title: Violence mars European football matches; Macron condemns Marseille clashes
items.summary: Violent clashes disrupted several European football matches on Thursday night. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

items.title: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italians; Iran denies involvement
items.summary: An attack on a Kuwaiti military facility killed two Italian nationals. Iran has been accused of carrying out the drone attack and denies it.

items.title: Narwhal tusk found to contain two intertwined microscopic spirals
items.summary: Using X-ray imaging, an international team found that the narwhal's spiral tusk contains two intertwined microscopic spiral structures.

items.title: New bionic hands wired to nerves restore sense of pressure
items.summary: A new generation of prosthetic hands connects to nerves in the forearm, allowing users such as Avi Davidson to feel pressure. Researchers are also using such prosthetics to study the human mind.

items.title: Virginia Tech converts PVC waste into engine-oil lubricant
items.summary: Virginia Tech scientists developed a process that converts discarded PVC, one of the hardest plastics to recycle, into a high-performance lubricant ingredient in three hours.

items.title: UN Security Council powers still split on next Secretary-General
items.summary: The UN Secretary-General's term ends this year, but major powers have not agreed on a successor, leaving little time for a transition.

items.title: Trump Organization partners plan Trump Tower in Hanoi
items.summary: Vietnamese partners of the Trump Organization plan to build a Trump Tower in Hanoi, according to sources cited by Reuters.

items.title: Study finds millions of South Asian wives lack protection from marital rape
items.summary: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but much of South Asia has not, according to a study.

items.title: Italy's late former police chief denied mafia inquiry allegations in letter
items.summary: An eight-page letter by former Italian police chief Gianni De Gennaro rejecting mafia inquiry allegations has been made public, days after he was found dead at his Tuscany home.

items.title: Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine's power grid
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia is preparing a major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Repair crews are working to fix damage from earlier strikes.

items.title: Hate graffiti reported at Golden Gate Park and Ocean Beach
items.summary: Hate-filled graffiti was reported at San Francisco's Golden Gate Park and Ocean Beach.

items.title: Strobe Talbott, former deputy secretary of state, dies at 80
items.summary: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who served as deputy secretary of state under Bill Clinton and later led the Brookings Institution, died Thursday at 80.

items.title: Erin Patterson files final High Court appeal in mushroom murder case
items.summary: Erin Patterson, serving life in prison for poisoning relatives with a toxic mushroom lunch in 2023, has launched a final appeal to Australia's High Court.

items.title: Indonesia weighs subsidised fuel price rise amid fiscal pressure
items.summary: Indonesia is considering raising subsidised fuel prices as fiscal pressure grows, according to sources cited by Reuters.

items.title: Study links screen time in infancy and early school years to poorer learning
items.summary: Researchers found greater screen exposure during infancy and the start of formal schooling was linked to poorer academic performance, learning and memory.

items.title: IMO works to strengthen search and rescue coordination in T&T
items.summary: The International Maritime Organization is working to strengthen search and rescue coordination in Trinidad and Tobago.

items.title: TTPS spent about $10M on overseas travel in five years, FOIA documents show
items.summary: The Trinidad and Tobago Police Service recorded about $10 million in overseas travel spending over five years, according to documents released under the Freedom of Information Act. Police say most was linked to security for the President's trips.

items.title: Genetic data suggests biodiversity decline in the deep sea
items.summary: Analysis of more than a decade of genetic data from five deep-sea fish and shrimp species suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be under way.

items.title: Family of teen threatens legal action after organs not returned after autopsy
items.summary: Relatives of 17-year-old Kieyanna Seechan are preparing to sue the State after her brain and lungs were reportedly removed and not returned following an autopsy at the Forensic Sciences Centre.

items.title: Padarath denies water crisis claims, warns of harsher dry season
items.summary: Public Utilities Minister Barry Padarath rejected claims by predecessor Marvin Gonzales that the government is concealing a water crisis, and warned of a harsher dry season.

items.title: House to hear reasons for ending Maloney closure and curfew
items.summary: Orders revoking the two-week closure and curfew at the Maloney Buildings Housing Development, which took effect Tuesday, are to be laid in the House of Representatives.

items.title: Prehistoric horned mammals may have had less sexual dimorphism than thought
items.summary: Giant horned mammals that emerged after the dinosaurs' extinction may have had fewer physical differences between males and females than long believed.

items.title: San Francisco commits $1.8 million to immigrant legal services
items.summary: San Francisco is putting $1.8 million into legal services for immigrants.

items.title: Maersk clarifies T&T port configuration for feeder cargo
items.summary: Maersk issued a clarification on its Trinidad and Tobago port configuration for feeder cargo.

items.title: Japan's JERA plans data centers near power plants for Anthropic and others
items.summary: Japanese power company JERA aims to build data centers near its power plants for Anthropic and other AI companies.

items.title: Study finds most neurons are multitaskers rather than specialists
items.summary: Analysis of recordings from 43 regions of the mouse brain found most neurons are versatile rather than highly specialized, challenging a long-standing assumption.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau junta postpones elections to 2028
items.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military government postponed presidential and legislative elections until November 2028, extending its promised one-year transition by about two years.

items.title: Former Spanish central bank chief chosen as next ECB president
items.summary: Eurozone leaders chose Spain's former central bank governor as the next president of the European Central Bank.

items.title: Germany arrests two Iraqis allegedly tied to Iran-linked terror group
items.summary: German police arrested two Iraqi men alleged to belong to an Iran-linked group said to have targeted US, Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.

items.title: First images released of DART asteroid deflection impact
items.summary: The first images showing the effects of NASA's DART asteroid deflection experiment have been released.

items.title: Karachi building collapse kills at least 4, with 17 missing
items.summary: A six-story building under construction collapsed in Karachi, Pakistan, on Wednesday, killing at least four people. Seventeen remain missing.

items.title: Violent incidents surge in Black Sea as Russia-Ukraine war reaches NATO's doorstep
items.summary: Incidents in the Black Sea linked to the Russia-Ukraine war have increased, raising concerns for NATO members. Romania's navy is working to fend off Russian attacks aimed at Ukraine.

items.title: Hong Kong marks anniversary of deadly fire
items.summary: Hong Kong residents laid flowers and prayed for victims of the city's deadliest fire in decades on its anniversary, following a government warning.

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases
items.summary: An Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has reached 12,000 cases. Fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting containment, and some responders have evacuated.

items.title: Kenyan court rules US-backed Ebola quarantine center unconstitutional
items.summary: Kenya's High Court ruled the government violated the constitution by allowing construction of a US-backed Ebola quarantine facility without public participation.

items.title: Kim Jong Un vows to build more nuclear weapons
items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited nuclear material production facilities and called for more nuclear weapons, citing threats from the US and South Korea.

items.title: Serbia sets early presidential election for December 27
items.summary: Serbia's parliament speaker set an early presidential election for December 27, after students won a parliamentary vote.

items.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel; judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech
items.summary: East Coast storms threatened coastal flooding and disrupted holiday travel. Separately, a judge ruled the FCC cannot punish ABC over satire criticised by President Trump.

items.title: Draining peatlands accounts for a few percent of global warming
items.summary: A detailed estimate going back to 1800 quantifies the carbon released by draining peatlands, finding it responsible for a few percent of global warming.

items.title: Ukraine says it shot down a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser
items.summary: Ukraine used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time, according to a senior adviser to President Zelenskyy.

items.title: Men more likely than women to ignore conversation while multitasking, study finds
items.summary: Men and women multitask similarly, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while doing so, researchers found.

items.title: Collapsing caves explain trenches on Australia's Nullarbor Plain
items.summary: Scientists found that trenches across Australia's Nullarbor Plain form as deeply buried cave systems slowly collapse upward over millions of years.

items.title: 345-million-year-old fossil reclassified as aquatic creature
items.summary: X-ray imaging revealed gills and thousands of tiny teeth in a famous 345-million-year-old fossil, showing it was a primitive aquatic or amphibious animal rather than an early reptile.

items.title: Rescuers search for miners trapped in flooded Indonesian gold mine
items.summary: Rescuers are contending with high water, darkness and narrow terrain while searching for miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine in Indonesia.

items.title: Sierra Leone sees steep decline in maternal mortality
items.summary: Maternal mortality has fallen sharply in Sierra Leone, though barriers to care remain.

items.title: Brine pools discovered more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
items.summary: Scientists discovered rare salty, oxygen-free brine pools more than a mile under the Red Sea that could offer insight into Earth's ancient oceans.

items.title: Waymo reviewing customer service after passenger finds loaded gun in robotaxi
items.summary: Waymo said it is reviewing its customer service after a passenger reported finding a loaded gun in a robotaxi and said the company implied it was his.

items.title: Kagi launches Gmail rival
items.summary: Search company Kagi launched an email service combining privacy promises with AI features.

items.title: Backblaze explains sharing customer information with advertisers
items.summary: Backblaze said it shares some customer information with advertisers but will not share users' backup or storage files.

items.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites
items.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites, which would increase the number in orbit roughly 50-fold.

items.title: Repsol and Eni back $2 billion push to expand Venezuelan gas output
items.summary: Repsol and Eni are backing a five-year, $2 billion plan to increase natural gas production in Venezuela.

items.title: Ladybird browser releases first downloadable alpha
items.summary: The independent Ladybird browser engine released its first downloadable alpha for Linux and macOS.

items.title: Etsy revises AI terms after seller backlash
items.summary: Etsy clarified its AI terms after objections from sellers; some say the revisions do not address their concerns.

items.title: Data centers drive a US natural-gas boom
items.summary: Rising electricity demand from AI data centers is driving increased US reliance on natural gas, MIT Technology Review reports.

items.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing T-Mobile and Cisco trade secrets
items.summary: Huawei was found guilty of stealing trade secrets from T-Mobile and Cisco and faces steep penalties, according to the Justice Department.

items.title: Rising Chinese political figure becomes latest target of Xi's purge
items.summary: A rising member of China's political elite who had hosted tech leaders and senior US officials has been removed in President Xi Jinping's ongoing purge.

items.title: GPT 6.2 Astra reported to solve a historical mystery
items.summary: A post shared on Hacker News describes the GPT 6.2 Astra model being used to solve a historical mystery.

items.title: New experiments broaden search for ultralight dark matter
items.summary: Scientists are developing new experimental methods to search for ultralight dark matter.

items.title: New estimate puts Russian military deaths in Ukraine above 700,000
items.summary: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine, according to a new projection based on leaked official data.

items.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide; Abrego Garcia leaves US
items.summary: Authorities evacuated a 5-mile radius before the Army disposes of thousands of pounds of lead azide. Kilmar Abrego Garcia voluntarily left the US after a nearly two-year legal battle.

items.title: Republican lawmaker seeks FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia's Huang
items.summary: A Republican lawmaker wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats, and whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was warned, before questioning him.

items.title: Euclid space telescope discovers its first comet
items.summary: ESA's Euclid telescope discovered its first previously unknown comet, about 1.3 billion kilometres from Earth on an unusual orbit.

items.title: Physicists trap and cool a single positron near absolute zero
items.summary: Physicists trapped a positron, the antimatter counterpart of the electron, in a wall-free trap and cooled it near absolute zero, enabling precise matter-antimatter comparisons.

items.title: Two men charged after break-in at Prince William and Kate's Sandringham home
items.summary: Two men were charged with burglary after a break-in at Prince William and Princess Kate's home on the Sandringham estate. Police responded with dogs and drones.

items.title: AI is straining US open records systems
items.summary: Venture-backed firms using AI to file public records requests are overwhelming small local governments, including towns where a single clerk handles most duties.

items.title: Canadian police identify suspect in teen's killing nearly 60 years ago
items.summary: Authorities in Canada have identified a man accused of killing a teenager nearly six decades ago as she left her job.

items.title: Armed suspects take dozens hostage in Cartagena supermarket
items.summary: Armed suspects took dozens of customers hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia.
